subject: health
unitTitle: Sexual Health, Disease Prevention, and Community Action
title: Correction and reflection: health advocacy and respectful communication
essentialQuestion: How can understanding sexual health, disease prevention, and community action help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: Respectful advocacy states accurate information, avoids stigma, protects privacy, and makes a specific feasible request to the person or organization able to act.
A safe communication plan states the limit clearly, recognizes pressure or danger, identifies an exit, and brings in adult or professional support when direct engagement is unsafe.

For health advocacy and respectful communication, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Complete a fact-checked community-health project with family review choices, private questions, and no disclosure requirement.
studentTask: Annotate a supplied fictional exchange about health advocacy and respectful communication: underline the stated limit, circle any pressure or respectful check-in, and write a two-sentence response that states a boundary plus a safe next step. Add when a trusted adult should enter the plan.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in health advocacy and respectful communication; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
